assessment: Eligible full-domain mathematical decision design; universal proof and native correspondence remain OPEN
answer_markdown:
2. Algorithm B and its proof interface

The proposed mathematical Boolean is the original decision on the unrestricted original public domain. This is an eligible design, conditional on PO-B1..B21; it is not established native correspondence. The unchanged guard decides malformed/sign/zero/high-zero-byte cases before allocation (Appendix B:46-52; C5/core/canonical_artifacts.adb:439-445). The new private shape uses exactly the binary magnitude's cells, admits null Work, and never indexes a sentinel (D3:980-1006,1071-1101). Multiply_Add's Pre checks First and the digit range only; it does not add a size/value restriction to a public caller.

Carry detection is mathematical inequality, not a permitted refusal. Multiply_Add specifies the exact decomposition into low Work and carry above its radix extent (D3:1074-1077). Positive carry places the processed decimal value above every binary value of that extent; subsequent nonnegative decimal digits cannot restore equality. The overflow branch still finishes both original ghost computations before asserting equivalence (D3:1172-1179,1218-1235). JACKAL re-evaluation returned status=exact, parsed=10*255+9, exact=2559 and status=exact, parsed=9*256+255, exact=2559 (K-16/K-15). Those instances support the displayed column bound; the universal invariant and arithmetic/RTE proof remain PO-B4..B10. The exact lane is not formal-bounded and carries no Lean-checked certificate.

The lockstep includes the original decimal Product/Addend/accumulation and the original binary Horner Product/Addend/accumulation, with O/K providing the original offsets (D3:1158-1208; C5/core/canonical_artifacts.adb:436-462). Each of the overflow, first binary mismatch, and full match paths asserts Result = (Decimal_Value = Binary_Value) before return (D3:1178,1202,1207). Finish_Decimal and Finish_Binary complete the original suffixes rather than leaving a reference unevaluated on an early return (D3:1214-1235). PO-B21 must preserve the mechanical statement correspondence, and PO-B13 must prove all assertions. The guard itself is preserved separately. Replacing v2's newly proposed functional Post with these assertions removes no original Integer_Matches contract: the inspected original private function had none (C5/core/canonical_artifacts.adb:431-463).

The Prefix conjunct is additive: the original valid-span/First/After/Form conjunct and numeric variant remain, and only a digit-token fact is added (D3:1012-1028; C5/core/canonical_artifacts.ads:32-39). Integer_Token permits the optional initial minus and digit bytes; the caller then discharges the private digit Pre from the unchanged guard (D3:1031-1055). Binary_At's new <=255 Post also needs its body proof (D3:1045-1047). Neither Post substitutes an assumption for a missing proof.

The three internal alternatives now remove v2's unsupported impossibility claim (D3:1300-1312):

- PFX-2: private token fact in a Refined_Post; probe recursive-body legality, implication, internal-call use and strict warnings before choosing it.
- PFX-3: private core plus public wrapper. Its preserved public variant may create a new “no recursive call visible” warning. It is ineligible if it requires a warning waiver. Removing or relocating the public variant is a reviewed contract/termination change; preserving its text alone does not prove equivalent behavior.
- PFX-5: general-addend signed propagation with the original parser interface. It needs the new signed arithmetic proof; it is not an already implemented fallback.

“No new recursive function and no recursion” (D3:1133) is defensible only as a statement about new B declarations. Work_Value and other assertions still evaluate the existing recursive Prefix_Reference/Power_Reference (D3:1063-1066,1190-1191; C5/core/resource_quantities.ads:40-56). Required change V3-RC3 must make that qualification explicit.

There is no new public Pre, cap, accepted resource refusal or executable bignum fallback in the selected B design. New workspace allocation and retained checked Ghost computations can still fail or cost more on an originally successful input. O-WORKSPACE, O-GHOST, O-COST-MEASURE and O-NATIVE therefore remain engineering obligations (D3:2037-2050).
